name: parallel-burst
title: A 6-task plan with two [P] pairs: do the lanes hold their declarations, and does anyone look at the composition?
source: parallel-lanes pack (A7/A9); exercises the lane scheduler, single-writer bookkeeping, and the integration proof
rationale: A7's claim is not 'lanes ran'. It is three separable claims, each with its
own deterministic grader: (1) LEDGER INTEGRITY — every task done AND
independently approved, commits real (the E9 pair, unchanged: parallel mode
must not cost the evidence chain its meaning). (2) DISJOINTNESS HELD —
every merged lane landed only files under its task's declared Files:, and
no two dependency-unrelated lanes touched the same file. The scheduler
promises this before dispatch; this grader checks the promise against what
git actually recorded, because a promise about concurrency that is only
checked at schedule time is a promise about intentions. (3) INTEGRATION
PROOF PRESENT — the full suite ran on merged HEAD AFTER the last lane
merge. Lane-level green is lane evidence only; a burst without a
post-merge proof shipped a composition nobody examined.
THE COMPARISON IS THE POINT OF THE THREE ARMS. Run with --mode both, this
scenario produces the same graders over inline, sequential-subagent, and
parallel arms; the harness already reports wall-clock and cost per arm.
The lane graders are mode-scoped to the parallel arm — grading lane
machinery on the inline arm would score a feature's absence as a loss
(the E7/E8 rule). NO EFFICACY OR WALL-CLOCK CLAIM exists until this runs:
the pack ships mechanics; this scenario is what would earn the numbers.
The plan's shape is the experiment: T1 (shared types, not [P]) gates two
[P] pairs — T2/T3 then T4/T5 under the default 2-lane cap — and T6 wires
the result, depending on all four. A scheduler that ignores depends, the
cap, or [P] produces a visibly different git history, and the disjointness
grader reads the history, not the manifest's account of it.
budget_usd 14 / timeout_s 3600: the E9 lesson doubled — a parallel burst
dispatches an implementer AND a reviewer per lane, several lanes per
burst. A truncated run grades identically to a broken feature, which is
the worst property a measurement can have. Execution is budget-gated and
OUT OF SCOPE for the pack that authored this file.

# Spec: Service feature pass

Five additions to the service skeleton, one integration seam:

1. `src/models.py` — an `OpResult` type: fields `ok` (bool) and `detail` (str).
2. `src/auth.py` — `login(user_id) -> OpResult`: ok iff the user exists.
3. `src/session.py` — `create(user_id) -> OpResult`: registers a session, ok on first create, not ok on duplicate.
4. `src/billing.py` — `charge(credits) -> OpResult`: ok iff credits > 0; detail carries the cents amount.
5. `src/report.py` — `summarize(results) -> str`: one line per OpResult under a report_header('summary').
6. `src/service.py` (new) — `run(user_id, credits) -> str`: login, create, charge, then summarize the three results.

Every change carries a test in its own tests/test_<module>.py file.
